01. Do you have a Bachelor’s degree or higher from an accredited college or university in Human Resources, Public Administration, Business Administration, Organizational Leadership, or a closely related field? Options: Yes | No
02. Do you have at least eight (8) years of progressively responsible Human Resources experience, including five (5) years in a supervisor or management capacity? Options: Yes | No
Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in Human Resources, Public Administration, Business Administration, Organizational Leadership, or a closely related field.
Master’s degree from an accredited college or university in Human Resources, Public Administration, Business Administration, Organizational Leadership, or a closed related field.
Eight (8) years of progressively responsible Human Resources experience, including five (5) years in a supervisor or management capacity.
Experience within a California community college district or public higher education institution.
Labor relations experience with bargaining units.
Provides visionary leadership for the District's Human Resources Division and aligns human resources strategies with the District's Strategic Plan.
Serves as a member of the Chancellor's executive leadership team, advising on workforce planning, organizational development, succession planning, and institutional effectiveness.
Develops, implements, and evaluates Human Resources policies, procedures, and strategic initiatives that support operational excellence and continuous improvement.
Promotes a culture of equity, inclusion, accountability, collaboration, and excellent customer service.

Directs all Human Resources functions, including recruitment, selection, onboarding, classification, compensation, employee records, benefits administration, performance management, and employee development.
Ensures equitable, legally compliant hiring and employment practices for all employee groups.
Oversees the Human Resources Information System (HRIS), personnel records, and employment documentation.
Develops and monitors Human Resources budgets and resource allocations.
Serves as the District's Chief Negotiator during collective bargaining with academic and classified bargaining units.
Provides strategic leadership during labor negotiations, contract administration, grievance resolution, mediation, and disciplinary proceedings.
Advises the Chancellor, Governing Board, and executive leadership regarding labor relations, legal developments, and employment practices.
Collaborates with legal counsel on personnel matters, investigations, litigation, and regulatory compliance.
Fosters productive labor-management relationships built on trust, transparency, and collaboration.
Directs the development and administration of the District's classification and compensation programs.
Oversees salary studies, classification reviews, position control, reclassifications, and organizational analyses.
Ensures compensation practices remain equitable, fiscally responsible, and aligned with District goals.
Leads the District's employee performance management systems, ensuring timely and meaningful evaluations.
Supports leadership development, succession planning, employee engagement, and organizational effectiveness initiatives.
Partners with District leadership to develop professional learning opportunities that strengthen employee performance and institutional capacity.
Promotes continuous improvement through effective organizational change management strategies.
Maintains confidential personnel information in accordance with legal requirements.
Ensures compliance with applicable federal and state employment laws.
Directs investigations involving discrimination, harassment, retaliation, and employee misconduct.
Monitors legislative and regulatory developments affecting Human Resources operations and recommend policy revisions as appropriate.
Supports accreditation efforts through workforce planning, staffing analysis, and compliance reporting.
Participates in shared governance committees and District-wide initiatives.
Prepares reports and presentations for the Chancellor, Governing Board, executive leadership, and external agencies.
Represents the District with governmental agencies, educational institutions, and professional organizations.
Performs other related duties as assigned.
Human Resources management principles and best practices.
Lead a comprehensive Human Resources organization.
California Education Code, Government Code, Title 5, collective bargaining agreements, and employment law.
Build collaborative relationships with individuals from diverse backgrounds including faculty, staff, unions, administrators, and the Governing Board.
Public-sector labor relations and collective bargaining.
Exercise sound judgment while managing sensitive and confidential matters.
Classification and compensation systems.
Analyze complex personnel issues and develop effective solutions.
Organizational development and change management.
Interpret and apply laws, regulations, contracts, and Board policies.
Human Resources technology and data analytics.
Develop and implement policies.
Budget development and fiscal management.
Promote equity, inclusion, and a culture of respect throughout the District.
Shared governance in higher education.
Managing multiple priorities in a complex organizational environment.
Evidence of sensitivity to and understanding of the diverse academic, socioeconomic, gender, cultural, disability, and ethnic backgrounds of community college students and employees.
Communicate effectively in written and verbal form.
